#### [Child Safety Using Optical and V2X Digital Alerting Technology to Bring School Buses and Students on the Vehicle Grid for Collision Prevention](https://www.sbir.gov/awards/215319)

_**Amount:** $748,172  **Topic:** 21-NH1_

This project extends the research and development conducted under SBIR Phase II contract 6913G621P800062 to develop and
commercialize two solutions for school bus and student safety:
1: A V2X (vehicle-to-everything) digital alerting solution for school buses that can alert oncoming drivers of a stopped school bus ahead. This is proven to increase awareness, decrease speeds, and reduce collisions.
2: An overhead optical illumination solution that significantly increases visibility of pupils crossing in front of buses in low light and low visibility situations, decreasing the risk of collision.

This project will include testing and adapting the devices to various configurations of school buses in different end user school districts, and environmental testing of the optical illumination solution to ensure durability.

#### [Common Operating Picture for Incident Response](https://www.sbir.gov/awards/209094)

_**Amount:** $1,192,489  **Topic:** AFX246-DPCSO1_

The proposed project under Phase II aims to develop a new capability for the Department of the Air Force (DAF) that will a enable real time common operating picture across civilian and allied fleets for disaster response, mutual aid, and response to Chemical, Biological, Radiological, Nuclear, and Explosive (CBRNE) threats and attacks. HAAS Alert is a Chicago-based small business that has a commercial solution that is currently deployed across over 2,500 state and local first responder fleets ranging from small towns to state patrols to big cities including FDNY and DC Fire & EMS, providing digital alerting and geolocation services via its HA-7 IoT transponder. This COTS solution provides safety alerting as its core service, and has been used for situational awareness and mutual aid. Major brands including Dodge, Jeep, Ram, and Chrysler are customers of the HAAS Safety Cloud data feed. Any time a CBRNE attack or natural disaster occurs, it is incredibly difficult for Air Force and DoD to maintain a common operating picture of assets on the ground - coordination is required with civilian or allied first responder vehicles that don’t normally share their location data with the DoD.First we will adapt and modify the HAAS Alert’s HA-7 transponder, currently installed permanently on over 2,500 first responder fleets, to create a rapidly deployable  transponder for temporary deployment on vehicles that are not already integrated with HAAS Alert's Safety Cloud to create a holistic real time view of partner fleet location.Second, we will integrate that combined Safety Cloud data feed into the SIGMA CBRNE platform to enable real time coordination across attack sensing and response.Third, we will integrate with the USAF fielded Tactical Assault Kit (TAK). The combination of these three adaptations will result in a first of its kind true common operating picture across non-DoD assets for civil-military cooperation during major incidents and attacks. Engagement with various stakeholders, including test range officials, information assurance officers, and system program office engineers, is planned to ensure compliance with DAF regulations and operational guidelines. Continuous feedback from end-users will be sought throughout the project to refine and enhance the solution’s capabilities.Through a subcontract we will leverage the expertise of experienced large business Two Six Technologies which has significant past performance working with the USAF on TAK and has developed the commercial SIGMA CBRNE platform which we intend to integrate into and create a joint commercial solution. This project promises to deliver a new and game changing capability for the USAF via a common operating picture for disaster response.

#### [Child Safety Using Optical and V2X Digital Alerting Technology to Bring School Buses and Students on the Vehicle Grid for Collision Prevention](https://www.sbir.gov/awards/195916)

_**Amount:** $499,993  **Topic:** 21-NH1_

Across the nation, school buses drive our kids to and from school, in rural, suburban, and large cities – all having the same problem: safely transporting school children. This proposal calls out (1) there is no school bus V2X solution that exists in any meaningful scalable way today (2) there is no readily available solution to solve for school children being struck during evening hours when visibility is low. It's not just school buses that have struckby issues, in fact, the biggest death and injury rate for police, fire, ems, towing, and construction is struckbys. Our team has built solutions with proven outcomes using V2X technologies and optical systems to prevent struck by vehicles in these markets. We propose phase I to experiment with these solutions to determine the best solution for children while being transported by bus.

#### [Open Call for Innovative Defense-Related Dual-Purpose Technologies/Solutions with a Clear Air Force Stakeholder Need](https://www.sbir.gov/awards/180409)

_**Amount:** $49,904  **Topic:** AF192-001_

HAAS Alert Collision Prevention for to United States Air Force (USAF) Emergency Vehicles (EV) to enable the future of base safety now. The HAAS Cellular Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) Safety Cloud allows for connected EVs to alert drivers and other EV when en route and on scene. HAAS Alert brings interoperable connected vehicle technology to USAF Bases today, leading the push to create the base of the future. HAAS Alert can connect to existing and future systems and infrastructure to HAAS Alert can connect vehicles using either proven, tested Internet of Things (IoT) devices in USAF vehicles or direct integration with existing USAF Telematics, CAD or MDT systems.
